correctness.rationale: Stable equitable WL/colour-refinement partitions can identify the unique line through two singleton points, the intersection of nonparallel singleton lines and the unique line parallel to a singleton line through a singleton point. The parallel proof is not a free logical assumption: points on the marked singleton line form a union of stable point classes, and among lines incident to P exactly one has zero neighbours in that invariant union, while all nonparallel lines have one. Cartesian constructions with O,U,V recover coordinate addition and multiplication, and extra marked coordinates; finite integral domain implies generated ring is the subfield K. Joining points gives every K-rational line. Conversely Frobenius x↦x^{|K|} fixes precisely K and every marked point, and moves all other vertices so they cannot lie in singleton classes. For q prime 3-frame generates the whole plane; if e>1 three marks are fixed by nontrivial Frobenius, and marking a fourth (t,0) with F_p(t)=F_q is sufficient. For <=2 marks and collinear triples an affine shear fixing marks prevents discreteness. Checked source finite field polynomial-basis implementation for q=2,3,4,8,9,16,25, and independent geometric closure verifier; infinite claim follows from construction/Frobenius, not those computations. Crucial distinction: this is singleton stable classes, not all non-singleton classes.

value.rationale: Natural interface of equitable partitions, algorithmic individualization, and coordinate subfield geometry; exact smallest marks and exact singleton counts provide a meaningful structural classification for all finite extension degrees.

final_claim: In the point-line incidence graph of AG(2,F_q), q=p^e, individual marks including a noncollinear affine frame yield stable singleton point classes exactly K² and singleton affine line classes exactly the lines over K, where K is the subfield generated by frame coordinates of all marked points. Counts |K|² and |K|(|K|+1); minimum point landmarks for discrete refinement: 3 for e=1, 4 for e>1.
limitations: Only finite Desarguesian affine planes, with individually distinct marked POINT vertices and a noncollinear frame.
No assertion on non-singleton class structure or uniform refinement-round complexity.
Verifier finite fields through order25 are corroboration, not an all-prime-power proof.
